title: Vanishing of all reductions from the first reduction
statement: Let l be a prime, E a finite extension of Q_l, and X any scheme. Work in the unbounded derived category of internal modules over the continuous integral coefficient ring O_E pulled back from the profinite point to X_Proet. The canonical reduction functor at index n is derived extension to O_E/pi^(n+1). Completeness means invertibility of the specified zero-nullhomotopy Roos augmentation on a K-flat representative. For every complete object K, if its reduction at index zero is zero, then its reduction at every natural index is zero and K is zero.

proof.text: Use the integral-reduction comparison and exact restriction to transfer first-level vanishing to reductionFunctor. Apply the successive coefficient distinguished triangles with m=1 and induction. Transfer all levels back using the comparison. Exact faithful scalar restriction detects vanishing on homology and hence on the derived category. Construct the product of the zero integral levels by its zero limiting cone. The normalized Roos triangle has two zero product vertices, so its fibre is zero. Completeness supplies an invertible augmentation, identifying K with this fibre.

lean.statement:
theorem derived_nakayama_first_reduction_vanishing
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : Type u) [Field E]
    [Algebra (Padic l) E] [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) E] (X : Scheme.{u}) :
    ∀ K : DerivedCategory (AdicCompletion.Modules l E X),
      IsDerivedComplete l E X K →
      IsZero ((AdicCompletion.derivedReduction l E X 0).obj K) →
        (∀ n : ℕ, IsZero ((AdicCompletion.derivedReduction l E X n).obj K)) ∧
          IsZero K
